item.content:encoded:
I hate the non-classic header.
It actively breaks my immersion because the colorful, graphic-design-forward elements just don't jibe with my experience of bureaucracies. Much less the particular cold and detached feel that is a core element of proper tone.

Yes, it would be an objectively better system in-universe. It clearly conveys more useful information at a glance than the one word designations.
But that high level of good common sense is a large part of why it doesn't click for me as something The Foundation would adopt. Real world governments still use terms and procedures from the 19th century, and combating any update to them is one of the few issues that unite opposing political parties. If anything, The Foundation's core mission of preserving the status quo would pre-dispose administration to be even more stodgy and resistant to change.

Which is a shame because it means I can't enjoy this piece, even though on an intellectual level I recognize it is very good and the sort of thing I should like.

It's like the neo-header is a 351 variant. Instead of inflicting memories without emotional context, it dictates a negative emotional response regarding the text it precedes.
